title: Auth/Audit Observability: SLOs, Alerts, and Postmortem for RBAC/SSO Pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-09 at ~22:07 UTC we observed a spike in SSO failures and a gap in audit log delivery for ~7 minutes. The RBAC v2 rollout had a schema-compatible change deployed earlier that day; a change in the audit-forwarder batching logic combined with a transient downstream backpressure event caused audit events to be delayed and, in some cases, dropped before retries were triggered. This impacted authentication observability: login attempts showed as successful to the application but corresponding audit events were missing for a subset of users, delaying incident detection and complicating compliance requests.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-09 19:40 UTC: RBAC v2 deployment (canary) completed for 10% of traffic.
- 2026-03-09 21:58 UTC: Audit-forwarder service received a configuration update that changed batching thresholds.
- 2026-03-09 22:07 UTC: Pager triggered for increased SSO error rate in eu-west-1. Initial mitigation: scaled audit-forwarder replicas and rolled back the batching threshold change.
- 2026-03-09 22:14 UTC: Audit events ingestion lag returned to baseline.
- 2026-03-10: Incident declared and triage started.

Root cause: A combination of (1) an aggressive batching threshold change in the audit-forwarder (ship to improve throughput) and (2) a transient elevated load causing Kafka consumer backpressure. The forwarder entered a path where messages were held awaiting batch fullness and a schema validation failure caused immediate drop of one batch. Retries were not invoked due to a bug in the forwarder's error handling path introduced during the RBAC v2 related refactor.

Impact: Audit event delivery for authentication and RBAC evaluation events was delayed or missing for up to 7 minutes for ~3% of active logins in the affected region. Compliance reporting and live incident detection for those events were impacted. No user credential exposure was observed.

What went well:
- Playbook paging and escalation worked; the first responder team assembled within 6 minutes.
- Canary deployment limited impact to a subset of customers.
- Quick rollback of batching change reduced tail duration.

Gaps identified:
- No E2E SLO covering audit pipeline ingestion lag and 99th percentile lag.
- Missing alert on audit ingestion lag; alerts were only tied to consumer lag but not per-audit-event-class latencies.
- Forwarder error path did not trigger retry/backoff for schema-related intermittent failures.
- Lack of tracing across auth -> forwarder -> storage, making it hard to correlate user session to audit event delivery.

Action items (owner — timeline):
- Define and adopt SLOs:
  - SSO auth success rate: 99.95% per minute per region (owner: PM-Security, due 2026-03-25).
  - SSO end-to-end latency (client auth request -> auth decision logged): 95th < 500ms, 99th < 2s (owner: infra-observability, due 2026-03-25).
  - Audit pipeline ingestion lag: 99th < 30s, 99.9th < 2m (owner: eng-audit, due 2026-03-28).
- Alerts to add:
  - audit_pipeline_lag_p99 > 60s for 5m -> P0 pager (owner: eng-sre, ON CALL).
  - sso_error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m -> P1 (owner: eng-sre).
  - audit_forwarder_drop_rate > 0.01% -> P1 (owner: eng-audit).
- Observability improvements:
  - Add distributed tracing for auth flow (id propagation) through the forwarder and storage (owner: runtime-instrumentation, due 2026-03-31).
  - Add per-event-class metrics (rbac_eval, sso_auth, session_revoke) with latency histograms (owner: eng-audit, due 2026-03-21).
  - Create Grafana dashboard and link to runbook: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/auth-audit (owner: eng-observability, due 2026-03-17).
- Reliability fixes:
  - Patch forwarder to ensure schema validation failures surface as retryable transient errors (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5893) and add unit tests (owner: eng-audit, due 2026-03-18).
  - Harden consumer backpressure handling and avoid unbounded batch waits (owner: eng-streaming, due 2026-03-20).
- Deploy/process changes:
  - Enforce canary + circuit-breaker for batching config changes (owner: release-eng, due 2026-03-22).
  - Add integration test that simulates schema drift and high-backpressure scenarios before schema/forwarder changes land (owner: qa-automation, due 2026-03-29).
- Compliance and audit:
  - Run a retroactive audit for the affected window and produce customer-facing summary for any compliance teams that request it (owner: compliance, due 2026-03-18).
  - Update security runbook with explicit steps for verifying audit integrity after a forwarder rollback (owner: security-eng, due 2026-03-17).

References and artifacts:
- Draft postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Auth+Audit+Postmortem
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/auth-audit
- Code PR (fix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5893
- Related tickets: ENG-4120 (kafka-consumer-hardening), ENG-4201 (rbac-v2-refactor-tests)

Follow-ups for leadership / PMs:
- Review SLOs and decide tradeoffs for stricter ingestion guarantees vs cost of retention and streaming throughput.
- Approve the additional pager duty for audit_pipeline_lag_p99 alert.

Owner notes: The immediate patch to the forwarder is low-risk and in review; longer term we should treat audit logs as a first-class SLO with dedicated SRE ownership. This ticket tracks the observability and post-incident work and will spawn the smaller implementation tickets referenced above.
